newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Dec 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Dec 19.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- LLOYD'S SLIPS ON 570 MILLION STG PAYMENT DUE TO NAMES
Lloyd's of London has admitted that it could not guarantee it would have completed payment of 570 million stg of 1993 profits releases to 11,600 Names before the end of the year.

Names have reacted angrily to the news, saying that Lloyd's is not honouring its agreement with the Names. This comes as Lloyd's prepares to sue, in the High Court, three of some 1,850 "refuseniks" who have declined to pay 500 million stg of losses.
-- WESSEX WATER CHEERS WITH SHARE BUY-BACK

Wessex Water has bounced back after being refused permission to bid for South West Water by offering to buy back 25 percent of its shares at a cost of 240 million stg. According to analysts, the announcement could mean a 15 percent boost to earnings and it will end the share-holding link with Waste Management International. The two firms' joint venture, UK Waste Management, will not be affected.
-- SHEFFIELD UNITED SIGNS UP CONRAD TO JOIN STOCK MARKET

Sheffield United has unveiled plans to join the stock market through a reverse takeover of Conrad Group. The 9.9 million stg deal will make most of the Sheffield directors millionaires and mark the start of plans to prepare for elevation of the team to the Premier League, which could double the group's seven million stg turnover. The deal will give 400,000 60-pence-stg share options to the Sheffield manager and club chief executive.
THE TIMES
-- JOBLESS BELOW TWO MILLION

A huge fall in unemployment has led to Chancellor Kenneth Clarke forecasting that Britain's economy will continue to strengthen in the run-up to the general election. Unemployment fell 95,800, the largest single drop since current records began, and the biggest monthly decline since after the Second World War.
-- WOOLWICH TO FIGHT ENDING OF TAKEOVER SAFEGUARD

The Woolwich Building Society has said it will fight to amend the Building Societies Bill. Woolwich said the Bill's proposal to remove the five-year takeover protection period for societies that become banks could hamper its three billion stg floatation. Economic Secretary to the Treasury, Angela Knight, has refused to bow to demands to retain the protective ring, which will be lifted if a newly floated society embarks on a takeover.
-- LONDON ELECTRICITY AGREES DEAL

London Electricity looks set for a 1.26 billion stg takeover by Entergy of the US. The deal will leave just two of Britain's regional electricity companies independent and without bid offers. The move will mean that half of the electricity supply businesses in England and Wales could be in US control. The Government has also cleared a bid by Dominion Resources, of Virginia, for East Midlands Electricity.
THE GUARDIAN
-- 432 MILLION STG BID PUTS OIL INTO TROUBLED WATERS

Oil and gas group Gulf Canada has offered 432 million stg for the British explorer Clyde Petroleum. Gulf said it planned to finance the bid by floating its Indonesian business next year, and said it had a one-billion-dollar bank loan in place. News of the bid sparked a flurry of activity in the oil sector with other small oil-exploration groups tipped as possible takeover targets. These include Hardy Oil and Gas, Cairn Energy and British Borneo.
-- POWER 'USURPED' BY OFTEL CHIEF

Roger Henderson QC, representing British Telecom, told the High Court that the director general of Oftel, Don Cruickshank, would have the power next year to break up BT's network even though this was not what Parliament intended. He said that BT feared that Cruickshank could use powers in a new licence clause outlawing any anti-competitive behaviour to force the group to dispose of some of its network. BT is challenging his right to assume the new fair trading powers through a judicial review.
-- NUCLEAR 'GRAND GOOF' PUT LEB BUYER ON BRINK OF FINANCIAL DISASTER

It has emerged that the US utility bidding for London Electricity, Entergy Corporation, came close to being taken back into public control six years ago after suffering financial difficulties over a 3.5 billion dollar nuclear power station project, Grand Gulf, which has been called 'Grand Goof'. Brod Bagert, former Louisiana Public Service Commissioner, warned British counterparts to "keep your eyes on your wallet". This disclosure will be embarrassing for the UK government.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- EU TO EXAMINE BOEING MERGER

The European Union's Competition Commissioner, Karel van Miert, has warned that the Boeing-McDonnell Douglas merger could be examined with "a fine-toothed comb" and he may impose sanctions if it hurts competition in Europe. He called the 45 billion dollar merger "complex and problematic" and left observers in no doubt that Europe could ultimately block the deal if the two US aerospace groups failed to answer competition concerns.
-- BRITISH AIRWAYS TO SEVER USAIR LINK WITH SALE OF 25 PERCENT STAKE

British Airways is set to sell its 24.6 percent stake in USAir, the American carrier, following conditional approval earlier this month for BA to forge a new transatlantic alliance with American Airlines. In accordance with the terms of the original agreement, BA has offered to sell the shares back to USAir but neither airline would disclose the price. The decision has heightened speculation that BA will accept the undertakings tied to approval for the alliance with American, principally that the two carriers surrender 168 take-off and landing slots at Heathrow to rival airlines.
-- BUOYANT CHRISTMAS TRADING GOES SOGGY

Retail fortunes have been mixed with better than expected official data on November's high street sales and an upbeat consumer survey on Christmas shopping being tempered by reports from shopkeepers that sales had slowed in the past two weeks. Nick Bubb, retail analyst at stockbrokers Mees Pierson, has said the mood in the industry has changed from confidence to gloom. Even larger retailers, such as Marks and Spencer, have experienced a slowdown in sales.
